pages.title: Ice Fishing
pages.text: The lakes froze. The fish under them did not all die.$(br2)Drill through thick ice and cast a normal rod into the hole.

pages.title: The Hole
pages.text: Drill where the ice runs at least $(bold)4 blocks deep$(); thinner ice has no water left under it.$(br2)An unused hole skins over and refreezes. The colder it is, the faster it closes. A bobber in the water keeps it open.$(br2)Use the auger on an open hole to plug it.
$(flavor)Hand-cranked. Field staff report this is the warmest they get all day.$()

pages.title: What Bites
pages.text: Through Phase 3, the usual catch.$(br2)From Phase 4, bites slow down as the water cools.$(br2)In Phase 6 the old fish die off. Expect bones.$(br2)Once the air is gone, something new starts biting.
Clear blood, no red cells, antifreeze in its veins. The everyday catch.$(br2)Late fish are slow to freeze raw. Cooked, they freeze like anything else.
Eyeless scavenger that eats the dead. Plentiful. Sometimes comes up with slime. Cook it.
Rare. Old. $(bold)Toxic raw$(), and cooking does not fix it.$(br2)$(flavor)ORSA Nutritional Services asks that you stop trying.$()

pages.title: Curing
pages.text: Seal raw Longsleeper in a $(bold)barrel$() with at least $(bold)8 gravel$(). Close it and leave it for $(bold)3 days$().$(br2)Then the fish is cured: the best food left on the surface, and slow to freeze.$(br2)Adding more raw fish restarts the batch. Hoppers do not count.
